title: Celestin saxophone section and the first Celestin session
summary: He lists the sax section (Earl Pearson, Sidney Carriere) and discusses who played reeds on the earlier Celestin session.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Who else was in that saxophone section in the Celestan band? Do you remember who else was in the band?
When I was playing? Yeah. Yeah. A Sydney career and I can't think of Pierce's last name. Yeah, he's been with Eddie Pierce too. Not the trombone player, I must be. He's a saxophone player.
Is he any kind to Earl Pearson? Earl Pierce, yeah, that's what it is.

But it's Earl Pearson. Now we got it straight. What did he play? He played saxophone. What kind? He was playing third saxophone, I was playing first, and Sydney career was playing talent. So Earl Pearson played alto then?
No, we didn't use it. We just had the saxophone. Just one? Yeah. I had the soprano though. I was the only one who used the soprano. Sydney career was using clarinet.
But what about on that first Celestan session though? How many, you know when you made Black Rag, Original Tuxedo Rag, and Careless Love?
Well, I don't think we had the big bands.
Who was in there? There were two saxes, huh? Two reeds, anyhow.
That was when B.B. Original was in the band. So fall back on it. What did you have? I think, and I was playing piano. Now I was playing sax. I don't know if sure enough it was Adolph Alexander.
Well, I've heard some people say Willard Tooney, and some people say, It could have been Willard Tooney, you know?

No, it wasn't a career. He hadn't come to the band then. It was either Willard Tooney, I think that's who it was. It was him or Adolph Alexander, probably it was Willard Tooney. So Willard, I got in the band just before Willard Tooney passed. Who used to write out arrangements for the saxophones?
